#Set up
```{r setup, include=FALSE}

# Load necessary packages 
require(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse, lubridate,  janitor, parsedate,  data.table, readxl,
       cowplot,ggpubr, plotrix, here, dplyr, purrr, arrow, zoo)

## Set a common timezone, so even if your computer switches timezones, everything is static
common_tz = "Etc/GMT+5"

```

## Combine all raw sontek files from Dropbox into L0 combined - only do this once!
```{#r combine data into L0 file}

##Dropbox shared url in case it is needed
# dropbox_url <- "https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/g6t7g8mcq64wtv9fwqxvd/AMqe_jDI5xyMf0T0tyEsbfE?rlkey=q6pcb76vybzko19uahrc5kgsy&st=jfy0ig2e&dl=0"

##Change path to your dropbox 
path <- "C:/Users/readz/Smithsonian Dropbox/Zoe Read/GCREW_LOGGERNET_DATA/archive_data"
#path <- "C:/Users/wilsonsj/Smithsonian Dropbox/Stephanie Wilson/GCREW_LOGGERNET_DATA/archive_data"

##Create a list of all sontek files in the archive
sontek_files <- dir(pattern = "Sontek.*\\.dat$", path = path, full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)

##Read in Sontek files
combined_data <- sontek_files %>%
  map(~ read.table(.x, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, skip = 1, sep = ",") %>%
        rename_with(~ gsub("velocity_x_zx_l", "velocity_x_zxl", .x)) %>% 
        rename_with(~ gsub("velocity_x_zx_r", "velocity_x_zxr", .x))) %>% 
  bind_rows(.id = "file_id") # .id tracks which row came from which file index

##Process Sontek files to remove rows with units, clean up column names, and set column types
sontek <- combined_data %>% 
  dplyr::slice(3:dplyr::n()) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
      # Ensure consistent types for datetime columns
      yyyy       = as.character(yyyy),
      mm         = as.character(mm),
      dd         = as.character(dd),
      hh         = as.character(hh),
      minute     = as.character(minute),
      ss         = as.character(ss),
      
      # Also force sample_number and sontek_id to character
      sample_number = as.character(sample_number),
      sontek_id     = as.character(sontek_id),

      # Parse timestamp safely (adjust if needed)
      timestamp = parsedate::parse_date(timestamp),
      datetime_raw = lubridate::force_tz(timestamp, tzone = common_tz),

      # Convert some numeric columns explicitly
      flowrate       = as.numeric(flowrate),
      stage          = as.numeric(stage),
      mean_velocity  = as.numeric(mean_velocity),
      total_volume   = as.numeric(total_volume),
      water_depth    = as.numeric(water_depth),
      index_velocity = as.numeric(index_velocity),
      cross_area     = as.numeric(cross_area),
      water_temperature = as.numeric(water_temperature)
    )

#write out the combined raw data file as a parquet file 
write_parquet(sontek, "combined_sontek_L0_files.parquet")

```

## Quick Visual Check of sontek other data - you don't have to run this it is just one year to see if we should include or not 
```{#r}


# --------------------------------------------------
# Define plotting function
# --------------------------------------------------

plot_sontek_check <- function(data, variable,
                              y_limits = NULL,
                              x_start = "2024-01-01 00:00:00",
                              x_end = "2025-01-01 00:00:00") {

  ggplot(data, aes( x = timestamp, y = as.numeric(.data[[variable]]))) +
    geom_point() +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(
      x = "Time Stamp",
      y = variable
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = as.POSIXct(
        c(x_start, x_end),
        tz = "UTC"
      ),
      ylim = y_limits
    )
}


# --------------------------------------------------
# Define variables and optional y-axis limits
# --------------------------------------------------
```

## Pull in RTK Data and add Water Elevation 
```{r}

#Read in the RTK measurements 
rtk_dat <- read.csv("Flume_RTK_measurements_202511.csv")

#We need to see about getting these rtk data relative to the NAVD88 and see what GEOID we are referencing to 

head(rtk_dat)

#Calculate the average elevation of side A, side B, and combined sides: 
bank_elevations <- rtk_dat %>%
  summarise(
    side_a_mean = mean(Elevation[grepl("side-a", Name)], na.rm = TRUE),
    side_a_sd   = sd(Elevation[grepl("side-a", Name)], na.rm = TRUE),

    side_b_mean = mean(Elevation[grepl("side-b", Name)], na.rm = TRUE),
    side_b_sd   = sd(Elevation[grepl("side-b", Name)], na.rm = TRUE),

    combined_mean = mean(Elevation[grepl("side-[ab]", Name)], na.rm = TRUE),
    combined_sd   = sd(Elevation[grepl("side-[ab]", Name)], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

bank_elevations

#overtopping likely occurs if water levels exceed the 0.3 combined mean 


#Pull out the elevation of the sontek bolt on the flume - see Picture: Sontek_RTK.jpeg for location of measurement 
sontek_bolt_elevation = rtk_dat %>%
  filter(Name == "sontek") %>%
  pull(Elevation)


## Stephanie J Wilson went to the flume and measured the distance from the sontek RTK point (bolt) to the sontek sensor 
##   Took the sontek out of the water and measured with a meter tape: 176 cm from sensors to bolt hole 
sontek_sensor_to_bolt = 1.76

overtopping_sontek_to_bank = 1.12

#To calculate the sensor's elevation which we can then offset the data for elevations we have to subtract the length from sensor to bolt from the bolt elevation
sontek_sensor_elevation = sontek_bolt_elevation - sontek_sensor_to_bolt


#Now we can offset the water level measurements of depth and make a new column in the sontek dataset called water_elevation_NAVD88 in m 
# This should be depth - 0.694 m 

sontek <- combined_raw_data %>% 
  mutate(water_elevation = (water_depth + sontek_sensor_elevation))

#Estimate what the water depth would be if there was over topping: 

overtopping_mean = bank_elevations$combined_mean - (sontek_sensor_elevation)
overtopping_sd = bank_elevations$combined_sd - (sontek_sensor_elevation)



```

## Add the QARTOD Flag column: will be 2 to start, then any missing data will be 9
```{r}
#The NOAA QARTOD Flags for real-time data from ADCPs are as follows: 

  # 1 - Pass - Data have passed critical real-time QA tests and are deemed adequate for use as preliminary data 
  # 2 - Not Evaluated - Data have not been QC-tested, or the information on quality is not available 
  # 3 - Suspect or Of High Interest - Data are considered to be either suspect or of high interest to operators and users. They are flagged suspect to draw further attention to them by operators. 
  # 4 - Fail - Data are considered to have failed one (or more) critical real-time QA Checks. If they are disseminated at all, it should be readily apparent that htey are not of acceptable quality 
  # 9 - Data are missing; used as a placeholder 

#Figure out the interval at which the data is being collected each year 
interval_summary <- sontek_subset %>%
  arrange(timestamp) %>%
  group_by(year = year(timestamp)) %>%
  mutate(
    interval_min = as.numeric(
      difftime(timestamp, lag(timestamp), units = "mins")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(interval_min)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_intervals = n(),
    median_interval = median(interval_min),
    minimum_interval = min(interval_min),
    maximum_interval = max(interval_min),
    most_common_interval = as.numeric(
      names(which.max(table(interval_min)))
    ),
    unique_intervals = n_distinct(interval_min),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

interval_summary

#Add a new column with the QARTOD Flags where if there is missing data it will be 9 and all other data is set to 2 (Not Evaluated) to start 
sontek_subset_complete <- sontek_subset %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(timestamp),
    .record_exists = TRUE
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    # Assign sampling interval based on year
    interval <- if (.y$year <= 2021) {
      "15 min"
    } else {
      "3 min"
    }

    .x %>%
      complete(
        timestamp = seq(
          from = min(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE),
          to = max(timestamp, na.rm = TRUE),
          by = interval
        )
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        QARTOD_flag_depth = if_else(
          is.na(.record_exists), 9L,
          as.integer(2)
        ),
        QARTOD_flag_velocity = if_else(
          is.na(.record_exists), 9L,
          as.integer(2)
        )
      ) %>%
      select(-.record_exists)

  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-year) %>%
  arrange(timestamp)



```


Lettered Flags (OOB, OOS, SSF):
## Lettered Flag data that is out of instrument range or out of service  
```{r}
colnames(sontek_subset_complete)

# OOB = Out of instrument's sensor bounds 
# OOS = Out of service, when the instrument is out of water or being serviced 
# SSF = Sontek system flag, this flag indicates that there is a system code in the system_status column 

#First let's change all the loggernet NaNs to NAs that won't get plotted: 
flagged_data <- sontek_subset_complete %>%
  mutate(across(
    where(is.numeric),
    ~ replace(.x, is.nan(.x), NA)
  ))


#We will flag any data points that are out of the instrument's range of measurement according to: https://www.ysi.com/sontek-iq-series?srsltid=AU7gw4V9OR8OS4z9cEPSgi8mUjNUTbEjEMFYlS4bUTbEAj5btu2cOoc9

flagged_data <- flagged_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag data as Out Of Range (OOR) based on instrument bounds 
    flag_depth = case_when(
      water_depth > 5 | water_depth < 0.05 ~ "OOB",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # Add OOS flags for depth OR specific date range
    flag_depth = case_when(
      (water_depth > 2 |
         
         #This date range there is just constant water depth data so it cannot be real - there is evidence of flatline for this time period - and needs flagged not sure what happened to the measurements at that time  
         (timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2025-05-02 11:00:00") &   
          timestamp <= as.POSIXct("2025-07-29 12:00:00"))) &
        !is.na(flag_depth) ~ paste(flag_depth, "OOS", sep = ", "),

      water_depth > 2 |
        (timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2025-05-02 11:00:00") &
          timestamp <= as.POSIXct("2025-07-29 12:00:00")) ~ "OOS",

      TRUE ~ flag_depth
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag data as Out Of Range (OOR) based on instrument bounds 
    flag_velocity = case_when(
        index_velocity > 5 | index_velocity < -5 ~ "OOB",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # Add OOS flags for depth OR specific date range
    flag_velocity = case_when(
      (water_depth > 2 |
         
         #This date range there is just constant water depth data so it cannot be real - there is evidence of flat-line for this time period - and needs flagged not sure what happened to the measurements at that time 
         (timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2025-05-02 11:00:00") &   
          timestamp <= as.POSIXct("2025-07-29 12:00:00"))) &
        !is.na(flag_velocity) ~ paste(flag_velocity, "OOS", sep = ", "),

      water_depth > 2 |
        (timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2025-05-02 11:00:00") &
          timestamp <= as.POSIXct("2025-07-29 12:00:00")) ~ "OOS",

      TRUE ~ flag_velocity
    ) 
  )

##How many are OOR? OOS? 

```

## Flag data when there are internal system status codes 
```{r}

#The sontek has internal flags that it will report if the data have problems 
# These codes are explained in detail in the sontek IQ series manual, but are briefly described here 
# The codes are additive, so a reported 5 means 1 & 4 flags are present 

  # 0 - No potential problems detected 
  # 1 - High tilt values, check IQ mount 
  # 2 - Tilt values have changed; IQ may have moved 
  # 4 - Recorder space low - less than 14 days remaining 
  # 8 - No valid depth data; check for debris or burial 
  # 16 - One or more beams may be buried 
  # 32 - Low battery voltage 
  # 64 - Internal recorder is full
  # 128 - Stage is outside defined channel; no flow data will be reported 
  # 256 - Invalid temperature data; IQ may need repair 
  # 512 - Low SNR warning (SNR < 10 dB)
  # 1024 - Velocity sample filtered - turbulent or low flow detected 
  # 2048 - Pipe Size warning, dimensions are outside of recommended range 
  # 4096 - Vertical beam range exceeded; pressure depth is greater than maximum vertical beam range 
  # 8192 - Poor depth warning 

depth_codes <- c(1, 2, 256, 4096, 8192)
depth_all_codes <- c(1, 2, 256, 4096, 8192, 8) #8 is added here 
velocity_codes <- c(1, 2, 16, 256, 512, 1024, 8192)
velocity_all_codes <- c(1, 2, 16, 256, 512, 1024, 8192, 128) #128 is added here 

# We will flag data if there is a non-zero system_status code, but if the code is 4, or 64 these are just warnings and we do not need to fully flag the data 

flagged_data <- flagged_data %>%
  mutate(
    system_status = as.integer(system_status),
    
    # Append Internal flag to depth flags
    flag_depth = case_when(
      !is.na(system_status) &
        bitwAnd(system_status, Reduce(bitwOr, depth_all_codes)) == 0L &
        !is.na(flag_depth) ~ paste(flag_depth, "SSF", sep = ", "),

      !is.na(system_status) &
        bitwAnd(system_status, Reduce(bitwOr, depth_all_codes)) == 0L ~ "SSF",

      TRUE ~ flag_depth
    ),

    # Append Internal flag to velocity flags
    flag_velocity = case_when(
      !is.na(system_status) &
        bitwAnd(system_status, Reduce(bitwOr, velocity_all_codes)) == 0L &
        !is.na(flag_velocity) ~ paste(flag_velocity, "SSF", sep = ", "),

      !is.na(system_status) &
        bitwAnd(system_status, Reduce(bitwOr, velocity_all_codes)) == 0L ~ "SSF",

      TRUE ~ flag_velocity
    )
  )



```


NOAA QARTOD Flags:
## QARTOD Flag data that is out of instrument range or out of service  
```{r}

# 1 = Pass - Data have passed critical real-time QA tests and are deemed adequate for use as preliminary data 
# 2 = Not Evaluated - Data have not been QC-tested, or the information on quality is not available 
# 3 = Suspect or Of High Interest - Data are considered to be either suspect or of high interest to operators and users. They are flagged suspect to draw further attention to them by operators.
# 4 = Fail - Data are considered to have failed one (or more) critical real-time QA Checks. If they are disseminated at all, it should be readily apparent that they are not of acceptable quality 
# 9 = Data are missing; used as a placeholder

#Similar to before we are marking points as Failing based on instrumentation capability / bounds 
QARTOD_flagged_data <- flagged_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag data as Out Of Range (OOR) based on instrument bounds 
    QARTOD_flag_depth = case_when(
      water_depth > 5 | water_depth < 0.05 ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_depth
    ),

    # Add OOS flags for depth OR specific date range
    #This date range there is just constant water depth data show evidence of flatline for this time period - OOS 
    QARTOD_flag_depth = case_when(
      water_depth > 2 |
        (timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2025-05-02 11:00:00") & 
        timestamp <= as.POSIXct("2025-07-29 12:00:00")) ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_depth
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Flag data as Out Of Range (OOR) based on instrument bounds 
    QARTOD_flag_velocity = case_when(
        index_velocity > 5 | index_velocity < -5 ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_velocity
    ),

    # Add OOS flags for depth OR specific date range
    #This date range there is just constant water depth data show evidence of flatline for this time period - OOS 
    QARTOD_flag_velocity = case_when(
      water_depth > 2 |
        (timestamp >= as.POSIXct("2025-05-02 11:00:00") &
          timestamp <= as.POSIXct("2025-07-29 12:00:00")) ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_velocity
    ) 
  )

```

## QARTOD Flag data when there are internal system status codes 
```{r}

#The sontek internal flags are used to attach QARTOD Flags

# SonTek code	flag_depth	flag_velocity	Depth QARTOD	Velocity QARTOD
#   0	            —	            —	          1/2               1/2
#   1	          SSF	          SSF	          3	                3
#   2	          SSF	          SSF	          3	                3
#   4	           -  	        -     	      1/2	              1/2
#   8	          OOS	          -	            4	                2
#   16	        —	            OOS	          1/2	              3
#   32	        —	            —	            2	                2
#   64	        —	            —	            9                 9
#   128	        —	            —	            1/2               4
#   256	        OOS	          OOS	          3	                3
#   512	        —	            SSF	          1/2	              3
#   1024	      —	            SSF	          1/2	              3
#   2048	     SSF	          SSF	          1/2	              1/2
#   4096	     OOS	          —	            3	                2
#   8192	     OOS	          OOS	          3	                3

# We will flag data if there is a non-zero system_status code, but if the code is 4, 32, or 64 these are just warnings and we do not need to fully flag the data 

QARTOD_flagged_data <- QARTOD_flagged_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Change the QARTOD Flag based on the internal flag 
    
    #Change depth_QARTOD to 3
    QARTOD_flag_depth = case_when(
      !QARTOD_flag_depth %in% c(4,9) & 
      !is.na(system_status) & 
      bitwAnd(system_status, Reduce(bitwOr, depth_codes)) != 0L ~ 3L,
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_depth
    ), 
    
    #change depth_QARTOD to 4
    QARTOD_flag_depth = case_when(
      !QARTOD_flag_depth %in% c(4,9) & 
      !is.na(system_status) & 
      bitwAnd(system_status, 8L) != 0L ~ 4L,
      #system_status %in% c(8) ~ 4, 
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_depth
    ),
    
    #Change depth_QARTOD to 3
    QARTOD_flag_velocity = case_when(
      !QARTOD_flag_velocity %in% c(4,9) & 
      !is.na(system_status) & 
      bitwAnd(system_status, Reduce(bitwOr, velocity_codes)) != 0L ~ 3L,
      #system_status %in% c(1, 2, 16, 256, 512, 1024, 8192) ~ 3L, 
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_velocity
    ), 
    
    #change depth_QARTOD to 4
    QARTOD_flag_velocity = case_when(
      !QARTOD_flag_velocity %in% c(4,9) & 
      !is.na(system_status) & 
      bitwAnd(system_status, 128L) != 0L ~ 4L,
      #system_status %in% c(128) ~ 4, 
      TRUE ~ QARTOD_flag_velocity
    )
  )
    




```

## Data Description 
```{r data description}

#Create a text file that has the description of the data - This ideally should match the text that is in the data READ.ME 

datadescription <- "These data are measurements of water depth, velocity, and temperature made at the Smithsonian Environmental Research Center's Global Change Research Wetland (GCReW) in the Kirkpatrick Marsh along the Rhode River in Edgewater, MD, USA. Measurements were made with a Sontek IQ series acoustic doupler current profiler (ADCP) at the GCReW Flume (38.87486, -76.5465) through which a tidal creek flows. The Sontek ADCP is affixed to a PVC pipe bolted to the center of the flume that extended to just above the sediment surface. Measurements were collected every fiften (2018-2022) or three (2023-2025) minutes and recorded by a Campbell Scientific CR1000x logger as described by Wilson et al. (2026). These are L1 data, where L0 would be raw data that is received by the logger from the instrument and L1 has been processed with programmatic quality checks for depth and index velocity that flag data out that is out of the instrument bounds (OOB), out of service when the instrument is down for cleaning or servicing (OOS), or flagged because the instrument logged an internal system status code (SSF). Additionally the depth and index velocity data are flagged with QARTOD codes (1=Pass, 2=Not Evaluated, 3=Suspect or Of High Interest, 4=Fail, 9=Missing Data) according to the NOAA Manual for Real-Time Quality Control of In-Situ Current Observations QARTOD manual version 2.1 (2019). The QAQC procedures and the code to produce these data from L0 are available on GitHub (link) and for further QAQC'd data (L2) are available via: LINK."


#write to a text file 
writeLines(datadescription, "L1_data/DataDescription.txt")


```

## Create Author List 
```{r create author list}

#Pull in the common synoptic authors list: 
authors_common <- read.csv(here("Figshare/", "SERC_LateralFlux_common_author_list.csv"))


#create a list of the last names you want to pull 
names_we_want <- c("Wilson", "Miller", "Noyce", "Peresta","Read", "Reynolds", "Rich" , "Megonigal")
order_of_authors <- c(1:length(names_we_want))

authors <- data.frame(
  order_of_authors = unlist(order_of_authors), 
  last_name = unlist(names_we_want)
)

#Subset the common list for the names that we want 
author_list <- authors %>% 
  left_join(authors_common, by = "last_name")

#if you need to add any other authors 
others <- data.frame(
  first_name = c("first_name1", "first_name2"), 
  last_name = c("last_name1", "last_name2"), 
  orcid = c("orcid_id1", "orcid_id2"), 
  affiliation = c("affiliation1", "affiliation2"), 
  email = c("email1", "email2"), 
  order_of_authors = c((length(names_we_want)+1):(length(names_we_want)+2))
)

#add in the other authors 
#author_list <- bind_rows(author_list, others)

#write out the author list associated with the data:
write.csv(author_list, "L1_data/AuthorList.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
